channel.title: Nicotine Science and Policy
channel.description: Daily digest of views, debates and discussions on nicotine science, policy, regulation and advocacy.

item.title: INTERNAL MEMORANDUM
item.description: An internal memorandum can reveal more than a public statement. It shows how institutions frame risk, manage uncertainty and decide which voices are treated as credible before policy ever reaches the public. In nicotine regulation, that matters because language inside the system can shape whether harm reduction is seen as evidence, threat or inconvenience. Transparency is essential when decisions affect millions of adults who smoke. (Published on August 10, 2026bysubstack.com)

item.title: Benefits of Smoking Cessation Far Outweigh Risks of E-Cigarettes
item.description: The central comparison is not between vaping and doing nothing. It is between the risks of e-cigarettes and the far greater harms of continued smoking. For adults who smoke, the benefits of stopping combustible tobacco can substantially outweigh the uncertainties associated with switching to lower-risk nicotine products. Public health advice should make that hierarchy clear: quit smoking completely where possible, but do not let fear of imperfect alternatives keep people using cigarettes. (Published on August 10, 2026byumaryland.edu)

item.title: The rise of illegal tobacco in Australia
item.description: A sustained rise in vaping alongside a decline in smoking tells an important public health story. Behaviour is changing, and policy should seek to understand why rather than assume all nicotine trends move in the same direction. When adults replace cigarettes with smoke-free alternatives, the potential for reducing smoking-related disease changes as well. The challenge for regulators is to encourage that transition while continuing to prevent youth uptake and maintaining strong consumer safeguards. (Published on August 10, 2026byabc.net.au)

item.title: Groups seek tobacco amendment bill recall
item.description: A coalition of tobacco control organizations is pushing for the recall of the National Tobacco Control Act (Amendment) Bill, 2025, stating it would weaken existing regulations and increase tobacco exposure, particularly for youths in Nigeria. They argue that the bill would relax rules on electronic cigarettes and other tobacco products, going against public health principles. Concerns also include provisions for advertising to young people and inadequate enforcement capabilities. The coalition demands transparency in the legislative process and urges alignment with public health obligations. Organizations and professionals are called upon to oppose the bill for the protection of public health. (Published on August 10, 2026bypunchng.com)

item.title: How Underage and Adult Users Transition Between Nicotine Products? | #GFN26ScienceLab
item.description: Nicotine use is not static; people move between products, patterns and levels of risk over time. Understanding how both underage and adult users transition matters because regulation can either guide movement away from harm or unintentionally push it in the wrong direction. For young people, prevention and enforcement remain essential. For adults who smoke, the priority should be making sure product transitions lead away from combustion, not back towards it. (Published on August 10, 2026bygfn.tv)
